title: Ansel and the Static
premise: Hazel Zhou is a clone of the murdered shipping magnate Ansel Zhou, created as a legal instrument to inherit the dead man's unsolved case — and his enemies. Fifteen years later, a cargo manifest lists a ship that never flew, carrying a passenger named for the woman who ordered the original's death. Following that ghost through contested orbits, Hazel discovers the murder was staged to hide a peace brokered between the fleet and the colonies, and that the message proving it still sits in the original's sealed vault. To deliver it before the truce expires, Hazel must ally with the killer's daughter and the crew who became his found family, sacrifice the inheritance that defines him, and choose whether to end the war as Ansel's echo or survive it as himself.
about_author: Mirabel Galloway is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals before turning her hand to fiction. She writes science fiction about people who inherit other people's problems, and lives in a coastal town where she keeps a telescope pointed at traffic she insists is ordinary.

chapters.title: Dead Letter Orbit
chapters.summary: Hazel Zhou hauls contraband seed stock through the contested Verge lanes, dodging both fleet patrols and colonial privateers while his crew treats him like one of their own rather than a dead man's copy. A routine manifest audit flags a vessel called the Meridian — decommissioned fifteen years ago, on the night of Ansel Zhou's murder — now listed as active with a single passenger: Vess Ardent, the name of the woman convicted of killing him. POV Hazel; beat of unease breaking long routine.

chapters.title: The Name That Shouldn't Fly
chapters.summary: Hazel investigates the manifest anomaly from a neutral station, discovering the Meridian's registration was renewed last month using Ansel's biometric seal — a seal only Hazel himself should be able to produce. Someone is forging his identity, or testing it. His engineer, Dov, warns him this smells like bait. POV Hazel; emotional beat of paranoia tightening around the fragile trust of his crew.

chapters.title: Inheritance Clauses
chapters.summary: Flashback-weighted chapter: Hazel reviews the terms of his creation — he exists legally only until the murder case closes, after which his assets revert to the Zhou estate trustees. Closing the case means erasing himself. He meets a fleet archivist, Ione Sef, who confirms the Meridian filed a flight plan toward the old colony relay at Kestrel Deep. POV Hazel; beat of dread: solving the mystery may unmake him.

chapters.title: Crew of the Long Haul
chapters.summary: A quieter chapter establishing the found family: cook-pilot Marisol's birthday dinner in the galley, Dov teaching the young deckhand Tam to splice cable, Hazel watching from the doorway, always half outside the warmth. Marisol tells him he's family whether he likes it or not. POV alternating Hazel and Marisol; beat of belonging he doesn't believe he's earned.

chapters.title: Kestrel Deep
chapters.summary: Hazel follows the phantom flight plan to Kestrel Deep, a derelict relay station where he finds the Meridian physically docked — untouched for fifteen years, yet its logs show weekly activity. Inside, a message addressed to 'the copy' plays: Ansel's voice, recorded before his death, saying 'If you're hearing this, they've started again.' POV Hazel; beat of grief meeting urgency.

chapters.title: Vess Ardent, Alive
chapters.summary: Hazel ambushes the real Vess Ardent — not the convicted assassin but her daughter, living under her mother's disgraced name to draw out whoever framed the family. She reveals her mother died in custody insisting she took the fall for someone protecting a peace initiative. POV Vess; beat of two people shaped by another man's war recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Vess shares her mother's hidden correspondence: Ansel Zhou had secretly brokered a truce framework between the fleet and the colonies, and factions on both sides needed him dead before it could be announced. The proof — the full accord, signed by both commands — sits in Ansel's sealed vault aboard the flagship Meridian's sister ship. POV Vess; beat of hope shadowed by the question of why it was never delivered.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Ione Sef contacts Hazel with hard news: the fleet and colonies are observing a fragile informal ceasefire that expires in nineteen days, after which open war resumes with new weapons on both sides. The timing isn't coincidence — someone scheduled the expiry knowing the accord existed. POV Ione; beat of institutional dread, the machinery grinding toward catastrophe.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghosts
chapters.summary: Hazel realizes the forged manifests were a summons: someone inside the conspiracy wants the accord delivered but can't move it themselves, and used the one person with legal standing to open Ansel's vault — the clone. But a second faction is hunting the same trail. His dockmaster contact is found dead. POV Hazel; beat of realizing he's a key both sides want to turn.

chapters.title: Trust Exercises
chapters.summary: Hazel brings Vess to his crew over Dov's violent objection — her mother's name is poison. Marisol forces a vote; the crew takes her in, and Tam, orphaned by the war's first bombardment, becomes her unlikely defender. POV Dov; beat of resentment cracking into reluctant loyalty as Vess patches the ship's failing drive through the night.

chapters.title: The Vault Problem
chapters.summary: The accord vault is aboard the fleet flagship Perpetual, currently in high-security refit — accessible only to persons with Zhou estate authority during probate hearings held aboard. Hazel must formally invoke his clone status, announcing himself to every enemy he has. POV Hazel; beat of choosing exposure over safety, the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: Aboard the Perpetual, Hazel faces the estate trustees — including Corwin Vale, Ansel's former partner, whose questions are too precise about the Meridian. Hazel opens the vault legally, finds the accord cylinder — and a second document: Ansel's will naming not the estate, but 'whoever finishes the work,' as sole heir. POV Hazel; beat of triumph curdling as Vale watches him too calmly.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Refit Bay
chapters.summary: Vale springs the trap: he was Ansel's co-broker who turned when the colonies demanded concessions, and he's spent fifteen years ensuring the truce dies with its architect. He seizes the accord, frames Hazel for sabotage, and orders the ship impounded with the crew detained. POV Vale briefly, then Hazel escaping through refit scaffolding; beat of betrayal by the closest thing to an uncle he had.

chapters.title: Static
chapters.summary: Alone, hunted through the flagship's maintenance levels, Hazel receives a burst transmission on an ancient frequency — Ansel's personal code — guiding him to a hidden backup of the accord in the ship's comm core. The title's static is Ansel's dead voice threading through live systems. POV Hazel; beat of communion with the dead man he resents and resembles.

chapters.title: The Crew Breaks Out
chapters.summary: Marisol, Dov, Tam, and Vess escape detention by triggering a genuine drive malfunction Dov had been hiding, forcing evacuation of their impound bay — then steal back their own ship at gunpoint, with Tam coolly talking past a teenage sentry. POV Marisol; beat of the found family becoming a fighting unit, each risking everything for a clone they met as cargo.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days, Spent
chapters.summary: Reunited with hours left before the truce expires, the crew plans the impossible: broadcast the accord simultaneously on fleet and colony command channels so neither side can suppress it. Vess volunteers to reach the colony relay; Hazel must hold the fleet-side transmitter aboard the Perpetual. POV Vess; beat of chosen sacrifice mirroring her mother's false confession — but this time true and survivable.

chapters.title: Vale's War
chapters.summary: Vale, exposed but desperate, accelerates the timeline by provoking a border incident to force early hostilities before any broadcast can land. Fleet squadrons scramble; colony militias mobilize; the first shots of the new war begin falling across the Verge — directly along the Long Haul's route. POV Ione; beat of watching the machine she serves choose war over truth.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax part one: Hazel fights through the Perpetual's comm deck, broadcasts Ansel's accord with both commanders' signatures fleet-wide, while Vess reaches the colony relay through debris fire. Both transmissions land. Commands freeze mid-engagement as signed orders surface proving the war's continuation defies their own leadership's sealed agreement. POV split Hazel/Vess; beat of a held breath across two fleets.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Comm Deck
chapters.summary: Climax part two: Vale confronts Hazel personally, arguing the war is the only honest inheritance — that peace built on a dead man's secret is just another lie. Hazel answers that he is the lie, and chooses to end it anyway, subduing Vale as fleet security arrives to arrest him on the strength of the broadcast itself. POV Hazel; beat of defeating the man who wanted him to be only Ansel's echo.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Signature
chapters.summary: The truce holds and formal negotiations begin, with Ione testifying and the accord entering public record. The estate case closes — which means Hazel's legal existence ends. The trustees arrive to dissolve his identity and seize the ship. The crew refuses to hand him over, and Vess invokes Ansel's will: 'whoever finishes the work' is heir, and she names Hazel. POV Ione; beat of law bending against those who wielded it.

chapters.title: Whoever Finishes the Work
chapters.summary: Resolution: Hazel stands before the trustees not as Ansel's copy but as the heir who completed what the original started — a legal person in his own right, with a name no one gave him. He releases most of the inheritance to the war's orphans' fund, keeping only the ship. Dov finally calls him family out loud. POV Hazel; beat of self-authorship, the price paid and worth it.

chapters.title: Long Haul
chapters.summary: Epilogue: the Long Haul lifts from the Perpetual's bay under a ceasefire sky, hauling ordinary cargo through newly opened lanes. Vess signs on as navigator; Tam runs the manifest now, and files a passenger listing for a ship that never flew — retired with honors. Hazel looks at a future with no case attached and finds he doesn't need one. POV Hazel; beat of quiet arrival: survival, shared.
